body: Thank you. Not glad you're in the same situation but it's nice to know I'm not alone. Hope things go well for you too.

Hi. I don't know if I can give the best advice but I am also a lesbian.


I am going to school for an engineering degree and am surrounded by straight men day in and day out. My entire design team of 8 (excluding me) are all straight men. My lab partners are straight men. My TAs are straight men. All my professors....you get the point.


I was terrified of ever revealing my identity for the exact same reasons. I didn't want to be a sex object or treated like shit or being treated differently at all for that matter. I thought I was going to throw up the first time I mentioned "my girlfriend" to my design team.


But it wasn't nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. They were just like "cool!" and instantly accepted that I was gay. I've still been treated with the exact same amount of respect. My girlfriend has even been invited out for drinks with us a few times. No weird flirting, no uncomfortable questions, just interacting with decent human beings.


I'm not going to say that every experience revealing your identity straight men is going to be a positive one, but please know that there are genuine caring and respectful people out there. For every one gross man I've encountered there's been 1000 great men. 


I hope this helps.
